text.p: Safeway Inc. said Wednesday it offered to buy the rest of Vons Cos. Inc., another supermarket operator, in a deal valuing Vons at $3.25 billion that will create the second-biggest grocery store chain in the country.
Safeway, which operates 1,050 stores in the United States and Canada, already owns 34.5 percent of Vons. Vons operates 325 stores in southern California under the Vons and Pavilions names.

"The combination of Safeway and Vons would result in the second-largest grocery store chain in North America, with 1,375 stores operating in 16 states, the District of Columbia and five Canadian provinces and sales in excess of $22.5 billion," Safeway said.

In a letter to Vons, Safeway said it offered to exchange 1.34 Safeway shares for each Vons share not currently owned by Safeway, valuing Vons at more than $58 a share. On Tuesday Vons closed at $43.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
A spokesman for Vons was not immediately available to comment on the proposal.
Safeway said it was committed to completing the transaction and will not buy more Vons common stock except on a basis offered to all of Vons shareholders.
The combined company would have the No. 1 or No.2 market share in each of its 10 operating regions, Safeway said.
